source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 18 October 1946, p. 6 ("Derry elections: nominations for county and rural councils")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: Unopposed returns from the Belfast News-Letter (18 October 1946, p. 6); the official notice of no poll is in the Derry Journal (21 October 1946, p. 6).

note: Triennial election. The county Londonderry polls were postponed; nominations were taken on 17 October 1946. Only Ardmore was contested (poll Thursday 31 October 1946); the twelve unopposed returns are recorded, including two new members for Middle Liberties and Lough Enagh. Filed on 1946-10-31, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Londonderry that year (confirmed); previously filed under 1946-10-03 (verification 5 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Middle Liberties' to Liberties Middle (13 Nov 2026, by the owner's rule for division spellings: the official or DED-map name where there is one, otherwise the spelling most rounds use): the DED maps of 1930-69 (LIBERTIES MIDDLE) spell it Liberties Middle. This round was filed under the spelling 'Middle Liberties', a form of the division's name it keeps as an alias; the old address (middle-liberties) answers with a redirect to this one.
